context.body: The bounded canonical source is Deuteronomy 4:1–14; its local speaker, audience, sequence, and literary form remain controlling evidence.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Moses calls Israel to hear and live, recalls Baal Peor, and says faithful practice will appear as wisdom to other peoples.
observations.label: Israel’s life and law are displayed before nations: action

observations.body: the mountain voice gives words but no visible form.
observations.label: Israel’s life and law are displayed before nations: response

payload.posture: Read Deuteronomy 4:1–14 as identity before the land evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: Israel is distinguished by nearness and instruction, yet idolatry is guarded against precisely because no form was seen.
payload.title: Israel’s life and law are displayed before nations
